title: Generalized XOR-Difference Baselines for Speck32/64 Neural Distinguishers
summary: Speck32/64 neural distinguishers learn extra features and outperform same-round Markov-based XOR-difference baselines; whether generalized XOR differences capture those features remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For $r$-round neural distinguishers on Speck32/64, the learned output features can extend beyond differences and yield higher classification accuracy than the corresponding $r$-round XOR-difference differential distinguishers. Pure XOR-difference differential distinguishers may be inadequate baselines because they are computed under the Markov assumption. Determine whether incorporating generalized XOR differences through modular addition and multi-bit constraints yields a better classical baseline and captures the additional features learned by Speck32/64 neural distinguishers.

scope.domain: Differential and neural cryptanalysis of the ARX cipher Speck32/64.
assumptions: Pure XOR-difference differential distinguishers are computed under the Markov assumption.
parameters: r: number of rounds in the compared neural and XOR-difference differential distinguishers
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether generalized XOR differences through modular addition and multi-bit constraints provide a better classical baseline and capture the neural distinguishers' additional features.

progress.summary: The source conjectures that pure XOR-difference differential distinguishers are not the best baselines for Speck neural distinguishers and identifies the Markov assumption as a limitation. It proposes generalized XOR differences with modular-addition and multi-bit constraints as a possible remedy without establishing that they capture the neural advantage.
citation_labels: Zhenzhen Bao et al., Enhancing Differential-Neural Cryptanalysis
